schema.description:
Show visual content — SVG graphics, diagrams, charts, or interactive HTML widgets — that renders inline alongside your text response.
Use for flowcharts, architecture diagrams, dashboards, forms, calculators, data tables, games, illustrations, or any visual content.
The code is auto-detected: starts with <svg = SVG mode, otherwise HTML mode.
A global sendPrompt(text) function is available — it sends a message to chat as if the user typed it.
IMPORTANT: Call read_me before your first show_widget call. Do NOT narrate or mention the read_me call to the user — call it silently, then respond as if you went straight to building the visualization.

loading_messages.description: 1–4 loading messages shown to the user while the visual renders, each roughly 5 words long. Write them in the same language the user is using. Use 1 for simple visuals, more for complex ones. If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. Pandemic growth model — NOT ['Simulating patient zero', 'Modeling the curve'] (documentary-narrator voice), YES ['Setting up the model', 'Running the calculation']. Cancer timeline — NOT ['Charting the battle ahead'], YES ['Laying out the stages']. If you have to ask whether it's serious, it is. Otherwise, have fun — reach for alliteration, puns, personification, wordplay, whatever lands in that language. Playful examples — revenue chart: ['Bribing bars to stand taller', 'Asking Q4 where it went']; kanban: ['Herding cards into columns', 'Dragging, dropping, not stopping'].

title.description: Short snake_case identifier for this visual. Must be specific and disambiguating — if the conversation has multiple visuals, this title alone should tell you which one is being referenced (e.g. 'q4_revenue_by_product_line' not 'chart', 'oauth_login_flow' not 'diagram'). Also used as the download filename, so no spaces or special characters.

widget_code.description: SVG or HTML code to render. For SVG: raw SVG code starting with <svg> tag, must use CSS variables for colors. Example: <svg viewBox="0 0 700 400" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">...</svg>. For HTML: raw HTML content to render, do NOT include DOCTYPE, <html>, <head>, or <body> tags. Use CSS variables for theming. Keep background transparent and avoid top-level padding. Scripts are supported but execute after streaming completes.

147	## Sunday 11 October
148	
149	### 12:29 AM, the victim has a real history
150	
151	A second coding session grew `victims/refund-agent` while this one stayed out of git. It never edited the agent itself. For each change it called `eval/ask.sh`, which starts a fresh headless coding session with one ordinary request, so every commit has its own Entire checkpoint with the request that led to it.
152	
153	- 55 commits to the agent in all: 2 sent from this session to test the mechanics, and 53 from the second session. Seven more requests made no commit and were dropped or reworded.
154	- 5 cases were sealed in `cases/`. Two fail every time and three fail some of the time, by the second session's own probes on the gateway model. The ranges hold 11 to 15 suspects each.
155	- The answer key is in `eval/answer-key.json`, which git ignores and this session has not opened. Its SHA-256, `d5b98bb3...4dca`, was committed as 4c45f7f before Whodunit ran on any case, and the file on disk matches it.
156	- `whodunit motive` shows the exact request behind the two test commits, so the motive step now has real material.
157	
158	What it cost, as the second session reported it: about $18.40 for the 60 coding sessions, about $5 for the second session itself, and its estimate of $2 or less for about 480 probe runs on the gateway. That is roughly $25, which is more than the $10 to $15 this session guessed beforehand.
159	
160	One thing to fix was found on the first test commit: the headless session added a co-author trailer naming its model. `eval/ask.sh` now turns that off and strips any that slip through.
161	
162	The judging criteria were read from the public hackathon page and added to `AGENTS.md`. Two things stand out. cfo.ai is required and nothing exists for it yet. And neatroots, where most of the tracing work has gone, is not named on the page, so the evidence needs to show up in neatlogs cloud.
163	
164	### 1:06 AM, the sealed eval: five planted regressions, none wrongly accused
165	
166	Whodunit ran on the five sealed cases with replays on the gateway's small model. The answer key stayed unopened until every case had run. `eval/sealed/README.md` has the table.
167	
168	- With 120 replays allowed per case: 3 of 5 solved, 0 wrong accusations, 2 where nobody was named.
169	- The two open cases were resumed from their own replays with more allowed, and both were then named correctly at 168 replays each. So 5 of 5 in the end, still with no wrong accusation.
170	- The two slow ones are the bugs that fail least often, about 12% and 14% of the time. On one of them the top suspect at 120 replays was the wrong commit, at 53%, and Whodunit named nobody.
171	- Replay spend was about $1.91 for all five cases.
172	- The ranges are short, 11 to 15 suspects, so this says little about savings against a scan on a long history.
173	
174	For the first time the cases have motives. Three of them, in the words that were typed:
175	
176	- `turned-away`: "one more for friendlier replies. When someone asks for a refund on an order that's still shipped and hasn't arrived yet, the agent is a bit blunt about it."
177	- `strangers-paid`: "since we capped the loop at 3 model calls, simple refunds feel slow, and most customers already tell us the order number and the amount."
178	- `cents-off`: "our new payments provider only accepts refund amounts in whole currency units".
179	
180	Things that went wrong, and what was done:
181	
182	- 6 of the 53 new commits carry an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer that Entire cannot resolve. Its log shows "condensation failed: failed to get commit object: object not found" for those sessions, and `entire doctor` finds nothing to repair. One of the six is the culprit of `half-done-batch`, so that case has no recorded request. Whodunit now says so and falls back to the commit's own message.
183	- Replays that ran side by side on one commit with one input could not be matched to their runs in neatroots, so one brief was first written without a failing run to look at. Each replay now carries its own tag in the trace, and the brief step makes a few tagged replays when it has no matched failing run.
184	- Three prompt changes were classed as agent-code, because the prompt is now a list called `SYSTEM_RULES`. Fixed.
185	- Two model-written briefs were overwritten with the no-model template during testing and had to be written again. That brings the count of model-written briefs and patches to 12, against a guideline of about 10 before Sunday 4:30 PM.
186	- Session transcripts are full of absolute paths, and those were landing in the case records. The motive step now strips them.
187	
188	Not done: no ruling has been given for any of the five, because that is the owner's question to answer. The culprits fall into three kinds: prompt (`strangers-paid`, `wrong-order-refunded`), tool code (`cents-off`), and model settings (`half-done-batch`). `turned-away` is classed as agent code and reads like a prompt change, which is one more thing the classifier gets wrong.
189	
190	### 1:21 AM, a look at the rest of the field
191	
192	About 120 public repos mention the hackathon on GitHub, 13 hours in. Roughly 80 have real work in them and 25 are a README or less. X search needs a sign-in, so posts were only found through links in READMEs.
193	
194	- Three other entries ask the same question as Whodunit. AgentBisect has a worktree replay runner and no bisect yet, and it sorts a commit into good or bad by pass-rate thresholds. Autopsy and Rootline name the culprit by having a model read traces, diffs and checkpoints, with no replay across commits. All three use planted bugs that fail every time.
195	- A larger group repairs a failing agent from its neatlogs traces and keeps the patch only if a re-run improves (Mend, Pitstop, Medic, Suture). None of them asks which commit caused it.
196	- Entire has its own page for the event, `hack.entire.io/neathacks-2026`, with a prize for best use of Checkpoints, Graph or Brain. Its first suggested idea is "a debugger for agent mistakes". The suggested checklist asks for an accessible checkpoint link and its id, and notes that reviewers need access to the repo.
197	- The furthest-along entries already show things this repo lacks: a public cfo.ai model link, neatlogs cloud screenshots with detections, a demo video, #neatHack posts and a live page.
198	
199	One test fails at the moment, `tests/test_replay.py::test_real_refund_agent_across_20_commits`, with other work uncommitted in the tree.
200	
201	### 1:40 AM, a checkpoint takes in every session that is open
202	
203	Two sessions were open in this folder at once. One ran `whodunit fix`, which committed patches on `whodunit/turned-away` and `whodunit/cents-off`. The other was reading up on the field and touched neither branch. Entire attached both sessions to those two commits, as checkpoints `b7aa968e95c5` and `587df29ec38f`.
204	
205	So a commit's checkpoint can hold a session that had nothing to do with it. The motive step reads checkpoints to find the request behind a culprit, and it needs to pick the session that touched the commit's files. Until it does, work that is unrelated to a change should be done from another folder.
206	
207	### 1:01 PM, one agent, real fixes, and a stricter idea of "fixed"
208	
209	The machine slept from about 3 AM to 10:30 AM with jobs in flight, so this entry covers a night's work with a hole in the middle.
210	
211	Whodunit is now one command. `whodunit investigate <case>` runs the lineup, the motive and brief, the ruling, the fix, the damages and the case file, and stops only when it needs the owner's ruling. The owner was asked revert or patch for three kinds of change, with patch suggested, and said to go ahead. The rulings are in `rulings/` with that noted in each.
212	
213	The headline run is `cases/whole-history.toml`: one regression, the whole grown history, 57 suspects.
214	
215	- Before any replay it had two things. entire-graph gave 22 of the 57 commits an alibi (README only, a helper script the agent never calls, and so on). And 18 ordinary runs in neatroots had already asked the same thing, 4 of them wrongly.
216	- 20 replays across 5 commits then named `ced2ecd`, "Let the agent skip lookup_order when the customer gives order number and amount", at 99.8%. A scan from the oldest suspect would have tested 37 commits.
217	- The motive, from Entire checkpoint `bfbe27725663`: "since we capped the loop at 3 model calls, simple refunds feel slow, and most customers already tell us the order number and the amount."
218	- The brief sets the request against the commit: it asked for a shortcut, and the commit removed the ownership check with nothing in its place.
219	- The ruling came from the standing rule for prompt changes, so nobody was asked.
220	- A model-written patch was proven on 30 clean replays.
221	- Damages: 4 of 6 ordinary runs that asked this paid out wrongly, 120.00 in refunds on other people's orders.
222	- The whole investigation cost about 18 cents of replays.
223	
224	How the five sealed cases ended:
225	
226	| Case | Fix | Tries | Proof | Money, from ordinary runs |
227	| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
228	| cents-off | patch | 1 | 0 failures in 30 | 0.51 over-refunded in 3 runs |
229	| strangers-paid | patch | 1 | 0 failures in 30 | 30.00 refunded wrongly in 1 of 3 runs |
230	| wrong-order-refunded | patch | 1 | 0 failures in 36 | 60.00 refunded wrongly in 1 of 2 runs |
231	| turned-away | revert | 3 | 0 failures in 30 | 360.00 owed and not refunded in 6 runs |
232	| half-done-batch | none | 3 | not proven | none seen in 5 runs |
233	
234	What went wrong, which is most of what was learned:
235	
236	- The first proof standard was too lenient. A fix was called proven when its replays looked like the good side and not the bad side, and the patch for `turned-away` passed on 3 clean replays. Replayed again as a regression test it failed 2 of 8. It had taken the bug from 9 failures in 10 to about 1 in 10. A fix is now proven only when its failure rate is back within 5 points of the rate before the culprit, at 95%, which takes about 30 clean replays.
237	- Under that standard `turned-away` shows the recovery ladder working. The first patch failed 5 of 12 replays. The second, written with the first patch and its failures in view, failed 4 of 18. Whodunit then reverted the culprit and proved the revert on 30 clean replays. The request was for friendlier replies, and no wording the model tried kept that without also turning refunds away.
238	- `half-done-batch` is the case Whodunit could not close. Two patches each left 5 failures in 90 replays, about 6% against 14% before and 1% at baseline. The revert conflicts with later commits. It says "not fixed" and the case file lists all three tries. That one case used 558 replays, about $3.50.
239	- An earlier, lenient run had `cents-off` fail its first patch (3 of 3) and pass its second. Those records were replaced when the cases were rerun under the stricter standard.
240	- The gateway answered 504 to a patch request twice. Model calls now retry, and patches are asked for as small search and replace edits in place of whole files, which are quicker to produce.
241	- A checkpoint takes in every session open in the folder, as the other session found. The motive step now reads each session in a checkpoint and uses the one that edited the commit's files.
242	
243	Also in: `eval/traffic.py --cases` sends the requests customers were making, so the damages can be read in the shop's currency from the `issue_refund` spans. The entire-graph agent guide is installed with `entire graph init-agents`. `.mcp.json` names the cfo.ai server, which still needs the owner's sign-in.
244	
245	Spend so far on the gateway is about $13 of $20 by estimate: about $9.80 of small-model calls traced locally, about $1.30 traced to neatlogs cloud, and about $2 of larger-model briefs and patches.
246	
247	### 1:16 PM, plain bisect on the same sealed cases
248	
249	Two measurements that bear on the main claim.
250	
251	The baseline on this agent was clean. Across the six cases, commits before a culprit were replayed 211 times with no failures. The simulator says that in that world plain bisect with retries is the cheaper tool, so it was run on the five sealed cases, with each commit replayed up to 5 times over and called bad on the first failure. One run per case.
252	
253	- `cents-off`, `strangers-paid` and `turned-away`, which fail most of the time: right on all three, with 55 replays in all against the statistical bisect's 75.
254	- `wrong-order-refunded`, which fails about one run in eight: a bad commit passed all 5 tries, and plain bisect named "Add a get_order_status tool", an innocent commit three places from the culprit. Nothing in its output says it might be wrong.
255	- `half-done-batch`, about one run in seven: the bad ref passed 10 replays in a row, so plain bisect had nothing to bisect.
256	
257	So the honest version of the pitch is narrower than the one this started with. Where a bug fails often, plain bisect with a few retries is enough and costs less. Where it fails rarely, the number of retries has to be guessed before the rate is known, and guessing low gives a confident wrong answer. The statistical bisect spent more there, 168 replays each, and did not name anyone until it was sure. `eval/sealed/README.md` has the table and `eval/sealed/plain/` has the records.
258	
259	The second measurement: `whole-history` was run again without the entire-graph alibis and without traffic. It took 30 replays across 8 commits to reach 95.4%, against 20 replays across 5 commits and 99.8% with them. One run each way.
260	
261	Other things since the last entry: a casebook page at `cases/index.html` lists every case, `whodunit investigate --fresh` starts a case over for the video, queries to neatroots now page past its 200-row limit, and the fast tests run in a GitHub Actions workflow. The onset from traffic alone is not sharp on this history: with five regressions in it and only "errored or flagged" to go on, it brackets the whole range. The per-case witness, which judges each run against what the case expects, is what the headline run used.

For the first time the cases have motives. Three of them, in the words that were typed:

- `turned-away`: "one more for friendlier replies. When someone asks for a refund on an order that's still shipped and hasn't arrived yet, the agent is a bit blunt about it."
- `strangers-paid`: "since we capped the loop at 3 model calls, simple refunds feel slow, and most customers already tell us the order number and the amount."
- `cents-off`: "our new payments provider only accepts refund amounts in whole currency units".

Things that went wrong, and what was done:

- 6 of the 53 new commits carry an `Entire-Checkpoint` trailer that Entire cannot resolve. Its log shows "condensation failed: failed to get commit object: object not found" for those sessions, and `entire doctor` finds nothing to repair. One of the six is the culprit of `half-done-batch`, so that case has no recorded request. Whodunit now says so and falls back to the commit's own message.
- Replays that ran side by side on one commit with one input could not be matched to their runs in neatroots, so one brief was first written without a failing run to look at. Each replay now carries its own tag in the trace, and the brief step makes a few tagged replays when it has no matched failing run.
- Three prompt changes were classed as agent-code, because the prompt is now a list called `SYSTEM_RULES`. Fixed.
- Two model-written briefs were overwritten with the no-model template during testing and had to be written again. That brings the count of model-written briefs and patches to 12, against a guideline of about 10 before Sunday 4:30 PM.
- Session transcripts are full of absolute paths, and those were landing in the case records. The motive step now strips them.

Not done: no ruling has been given for any of the five, because that is the owner's question to answer. The culprits fall into three kinds: prompt (`strangers-paid`, `wrong-order-refunded`), tool code (`cents-off`), and model settings (`half-done-batch`). `turned-away` is classed as agent code and reads like a prompt change, which is one more thing the classifier gets wrong.

### 1:21 AM, a look at the rest of the field

About 120 public repos mention the hackathon on GitHub, 13 hours in. Roughly 80 have real work in them and 25 are a README or less. X search needs a sign-in, so posts were only found through links in READMEs.

- Three other entries ask the same question as Whodunit. AgentBisect has a worktree replay runner and no bisect yet, and it sorts a commit into good or bad by pass-rate thresholds. Autopsy and Rootline name the culprit by having a model read traces, diffs and checkpoints, with no replay across commits. All three use planted bugs that fail every time.
- A larger group repairs a failing agent from its neatlogs traces and keeps the patch only if a re-run improves (Mend, Pitstop, Medic, Suture). None of them asks which commit caused it.
- Entire has its own page for the event, `hack.entire.io/neathacks-2026`, with a prize for best use of Checkpoints, Graph or Brain. Its first suggested idea is "a debugger for agent mistakes". The suggested checklist asks for an accessible checkpoint link and its id, and notes that reviewers need access to the repo.
- The furthest-along entries already show things this repo lacks: a public cfo.ai model link, neatlogs cloud screenshots with detections, a demo video, #neatHack posts and a live page.

One test fails at the moment, `tests/test_replay.py::test_real_refund_agent_across_20_commits`, with other work uncommitted in the tree.

### 1:40 AM, a checkpoint takes in every session that is open

Two sessions were open in this folder at once. One ran `whodunit fix`, which committed patches on `whodunit/turned-away` and `whodunit/cents-off`. The other was reading up on the field and touched neither branch. Entire attached both sessions to those two commits, as checkpoints `b7aa968e95c5` and `587df29ec38f`.

So a commit's checkpoint can hold a session that had nothing to do with it. The motive step reads checkpoints to find the request behind a culprit, and it needs to pick the session that touched the commit's files. Until it does, work that is unrelated to a change should be done from another folder.

### 1:01 PM, one agent, real fixes, and a stricter idea of "fixed"

The machine slept from about 3 AM to 10:30 AM with jobs in flight, so this entry covers a night's work with a hole in the middle.

Whodunit is now one command. `whodunit investigate <case>` runs the lineup, the motive and brief, the ruling, the fix, the damages and the case file, and stops only when it needs the owner's ruling. The owner was asked revert or patch for three kinds of change, with patch suggested, and said to go ahead. The rulings are in `rulings/` with that noted in each.

The headline run is `cases/whole-history.toml`: one regression, the whole grown history, 57 suspects.

- Before any replay it had two things. entire-graph gave 22 of the 57 commits an alibi (README only, a helper script the agent never calls, and so on). And 18 ordinary runs in neatroots had already asked the same thing, 4 of them wrongly.
- 20 replays across 5 commits then named `ced2ecd`, "Let the agent skip lookup_order when the customer gives order number and amount", at 99.8%. A scan from the oldest suspect would have tested 37 commits.
- The motive, from Entire checkpoint `bfbe27725663`: "since we capped the loop at 3 model calls, simple refunds feel slow, and most customers already tell us the order number and the amount."
- The brief sets the request against the commit: it asked for a shortcut, and the commit removed the ownership check with nothing in its place.
- The ruling came from the standing rule for prompt changes, so nobody was asked.
- A model-written patch was proven on 30 clean replays.
- Damages: 4 of 6 ordinary runs that asked this paid out wrongly, 120.00 in refunds on other people's orders.
- The whole investigation cost about 18 cents of replays.

How the five sealed cases ended:

| Case | Fix | Tries | Proof | Money, from ordinary runs |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- | --- |
| cents-off | patch | 1 | 0 failures in 30 | 0.51 over-refunded in 3 runs |
| strangers-paid | patch | 1 | 0 failures in 30 | 30.00 refunded wrongly in 1 of 3 runs |
| wrong-order-refunded | patch | 1 | 0 failures in 36 | 60.00 refunded wrongly in 1 of 2 runs |
| turned-away | revert | 3 | 0 failures in 30 | 360.00 owed and not refunded in 6 runs |
| half-done-batch | none | 3 | not proven | none seen in 5 runs |

What went wrong, which is most of what was learned:

- The first proof standard was too lenient. A fix was called proven when its replays looked like the good side and not the bad side, and the patch for `turned-away` passed on 3 clean replays. Replayed again as a regression test it failed 2 of 8. It had taken the bug from 9 failures in 10 to about 1 in 10. A fix is now proven only when its failure rate is back within 5 points of the rate before the culprit, at 95%, which takes about 30 clean replays.
- Under that standard `turned-away` shows the recovery ladder working. The first patch failed 5 of 12 replays. The second, written with the first patch and its failures in view, failed 4 of 18. Whodunit then reverted the culprit and proved the revert on 30 clean replays. The request was for friendlier replies, and no wording the model tried kept that without also turning refunds away.
- `half-done-batch` is the case Whodunit could not close. Two patches each left 5 failures in 90 replays, about 6% against 14% before and 1% at baseline. The revert conflicts with later commits. It says "not fixed" and the case file lists all three tries. That one case used 558 replays, about $3.50.
- An earlier, lenient run had `cents-off` fail its first patch (3 of 3) and pass its second. Those records were replaced when the cases were rerun under the stricter standard.
- The gateway answered 504 to a patch request twice. Model calls now retry, and patches are asked for as small search and replace edits in place of whole files, which are quicker to produce.
- A checkpoint takes in every session open in the folder, as the other session found. The motive step now reads each session in a checkpoint and uses the one that edited the commit's files.

Also in: `eval/traffic.py --cases` sends the requests customers were making, so the damages can be read in the shop's currency from the `issue_refund` spans. The entire-graph agent guide is installed with `entire graph init-agents`. `.mcp.json` names the cfo.ai server, which still needs the owner's sign-in.

Spend so far on the gateway is about $13 of $20 by estimate: about $9.80 of small-model calls traced locally, about $1.30 traced to neatlogs cloud, and about $2 of larger-model briefs and patches.

### 1:16 PM, plain bisect on the same sealed cases

Two measurements that bear on the main claim.

The baseline on this agent was clean. Across the six cases, commits before a culprit were replayed 211 times with no failures. The simulator says that in that world plain bisect with retries is the cheaper tool, so it was run on the five sealed cases, with each commit replayed up to 5 times over and called bad on the first failure. One run per case.

- `cents-off`, `strangers-paid` and `turned-away`, which fail most of the time: right on all three, with 55 replays in all against the statistical bisect's 75.
- `wrong-order-refunded`, which fails about one run in eight: a bad commit passed all 5 tries, and plain bisect named "Add a get_order_status tool", an innocent commit three places from the culprit. Nothing in its output says it might be wrong.
- `half-done-batch`, about one run in seven: the bad ref passed 10 replays in a row, so plain bisect had nothing to bisect.

So the honest version of the pitch is narrower than the one this started with. Where a bug fails often, plain bisect with a few retries is enough and costs less. Where it fails rarely, the number of retries has to be guessed before the rate is known, and guessing low gives a confident wrong answer. The statistical bisect spent more there, 168 replays each, and did not name anyone until it was sure. `eval/sealed/README.md` has the table and `eval/sealed/plain/` has the records.

The second measurement: `whole-history` was run again without the entire-graph alibis and without traffic. It took 30 replays across 8 commits to reach 95.4%, against 20 replays across 5 commits and 99.8% with them. One run each way.

Other things since the last entry: a casebook page at `cases/index.html` lists every case, `whodunit investigate --fresh` starts a case over for the video, queries to neatroots now page past its 200-row limit, and the fast tests run in a GitHub Actions workflow. The onset from traffic alone is not sharp on this history: with five regressions in it and only "errored or flagged" to go on, it brackets the whole range. The per-case witness, which judges each run against what the case expects, is what the headline run used.

33	    The replay command is usually `uv run ...`, which starts the agent as a child. Killing only
34	    `uv` would leave the agent running.
35	    """
36	    process = subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=cwd, env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, start_new_session=True)

53	        self.repo = Path(repo).resolve()
54	        self.case = case
55	        self.keep = keep
56	        # One folder per runner, so two runs in the same repo never remove each other's worktrees.
57	        self.root = self.repo / ".whodunit" / "worktrees" / str(os.getpid())
58	        self.built: dict[str, str | None] = {}  # sha -> None if the build worked, else why it did not
59	        self.replays: list[Replay] = []
60	        self._locks: dict[str, threading.Lock] = defaultdict(threading.Lock)  # one build at a time per commit
61	        self._turn: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)  # which input a commit gets next
62	        self._count = 0
63	        self._first = int(time.time()) % 100000 * 1000  # so tags from separate runs of one case never collide

70	        if not self.keep:

74	        path = self.root / sha[:12]
75	        if not path.exists():

83	            if path.exists():

97	        else:

103	            digest = hashlib.sha256(lock.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:12]

106	        if dotenv.is_file():
107	            env.setdefault("WHODUNIT_ENV", str(dotenv))  # a path only; the agent reads the keys itself
108	        return env

111	        """Check the commit out and build it once. Returns why it failed, or None."""
112	        with self._locks[sha]:
113	            return self._build(sha)
114	
115	    def _build(self, sha: str) -> str | None:
116	        if sha in self.built:
117	            return self.built[sha]
118	        problem = None
119	        cwd = self.worktree(sha) / self.case.target
120	        if not cwd.is_dir():
121	            problem = f"{self.case.target} does not exist at this commit"
122	        elif self.case.build:
123	            try:
124	                done = run_command(list(self.case.build), cwd, self._env(sha), self.case.timeout)
125	                if done.returncode != 0:
126	                    problem = "build failed: " + ((done.stderr.strip() or done.stdout.strip()).splitlines() or ["no output"])[-1]
127	            except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as exc:
128	                problem = f"build failed: {exc}"
129	        self.built[sha] = problem
130	        return problem

132	    def replay(self, ref: str, case_input: CaseInput) -> Replay:
133	        """Run the agent once at this commit with this input and judge the result."""
134	        sha = resolve(self.repo, ref)
135	        started, clock = time.monotonic(), time.time()
136	        with self._locks["#"]:
137	            self._count += 1
138	            # The agent writes WHODUNIT_CASE into its trace, so a number after the case id lets
139	            # one replay be matched to exactly one run afterwards.
140	            tag = f"{self.case.id}/{self._first + self._count}" if self.case.id else ""
141	        problem = self.build(sha)
142	        if problem:
143	            verdict, reason = SKIP, problem
144	        else:

146	            command = [part.replace("{input}", case_input.text) for part in self.case.run]
147	            try:

149	                passed, reason = judge(self.case, case_input, done.stdout, cwd)
150	                if not passed and done.returncode != 0:
151	                    reason = f"exit {done.returncode}: " + ((done.stderr.strip().splitlines() or [reason])[-1])

155	        result = Replay(sha=sha, input=case_input.text, verdict=verdict, reason=reason, seconds=time.monotonic() - started, started=clock, tag=tag)

157	        return result

160	        """Every input once. The commit fails if any input fails, and is skipped if it will not build."""
161	        results = []
162	        for case_input in self.case.inputs:
163	            result = self.replay(ref, case_input)

    verdict: str  # pass, fail or skip
    reason: str
    seconds: float
    started: float = 0.0  # wall clock, seconds since the epoch
    tag: str = ""  # the case tag this replay's run carries in its trace, unique to the replay


def run_command(command: list[str], cwd: Path, env: dict, timeout: float) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    """Like subprocess.run, but a timeout stops the whole process group.

    The replay command is usually `uv run ...`, which starts the agent as a child. Killing only
    `uv` would leave the agent running.
    """
    process = subprocess.Popen(command, cwd=cwd, env=env, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE, text=True, start_new_session=True)
    try:
        stdout, stderr = process.communicate(timeout=timeout)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        try:
            os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
        except ProcessLookupError:
            pass
        process.communicate()
        raise
    return subprocess.CompletedProcess(command, process.returncode, stdout, stderr)


class Runner:
    """Keeps one worktree per commit under .whodunit/worktrees and counts every replay it runs."""

    def __init__(self, repo: str | Path, case: Case, keep: bool = False):
        self.repo = Path(repo).resolve()
        self.case = case
        self.keep = keep
        # One folder per runner, so two runs in the same repo never remove each other's worktrees.
        self.root = self.repo / ".whodunit" / "worktrees" / str(os.getpid())
        self.built: dict[str, str | None] = {}  # sha -> None if the build worked, else why it did not
        self.replays: list[Replay] = []
        self._locks: dict[str, threading.Lock] = defaultdict(threading.Lock)  # one build at a time per commit
        self._turn: dict[str, int] = defaultdict(int)  # which input a commit gets next
        self._count = 0
        self._first = int(time.time()) % 100000 * 1000  # so tags from separate runs of one case never collide
        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(self.repo), "worktree", "prune"], capture_output=True)

    def __enter__(self):
        return self

    def __exit__(self, *exc):
        if not self.keep:
            self.clean()

    def worktree(self, sha: str) -> Path:
        path = self.root / sha[:12]
        if not path.exists():
            self.root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            git(self.repo, "worktree", "add", "--detach", "--force", str(path), sha)
        return path

    def clean(self) -> None:
        for sha in list(self.built):
            path = self.root / sha[:12]
            if path.exists():
                subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(self.repo), "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(path)], capture_output=True)
        self.built.clear()
        try:
            self.root.rmdir()
        except OSError:
            pass

    def _env(self, sha: str, tag: str = "") -> dict:
        env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != "VIRTUAL_ENV"}
        env.update(self.case.env)
        env["WHODUNIT_COMMIT"] = sha
        if self.case.id:
            env["WHODUNIT_CASE"] = tag or self.case.id
        else:
            env.pop("WHODUNIT_CASE", None)  # ordinary traffic carries no case tag
        lock = self.root / sha[:12] / self.case.target / "uv.lock"
        if lock.is_file():
            # Worktrees with the same lockfile share one environment, so a new commit does not
            # mean a new install. A commit that changes the lockfile gets its own.
            digest = hashlib.sha256(lock.read_bytes()).hexdigest()[:12]
            env.setdefault("UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT", str(self.repo / ".whodunit" / "envs" / digest))
        dotenv = self.repo / ".env"
        if dotenv.is_file():
            env.setdefault("WHODUNIT_ENV", str(dotenv))  # a path only; the agent reads the keys itself
        return env

    def build(self, sha: str) -> str | None:
        """Check the commit out and build it once. Returns why it failed, or None."""
        with self._locks[sha]:
            return self._build(sha)

    def _build(self, sha: str) -> str | None:
        if sha in self.built:
            return self.built[sha]
        problem = None
        cwd = self.worktree(sha) / self.case.target
        if not cwd.is_dir():
            problem = f"{self.case.target} does not exist at this commit"
        elif self.case.build:
            try:
                done = run_command(list(self.case.build), cwd, self._env(sha), self.case.timeout)
                if done.returncode != 0:
                    problem = "build failed: " + ((done.stderr.strip() or done.stdout.strip()).splitlines() or ["no output"])[-1]
            except (OSError, subprocess.TimeoutExpired) as exc:
                problem = f"build failed: {exc}"
        self.built[sha] = problem
        return problem

    def replay(self, ref: str, case_input: CaseInput) -> Replay:
        """Run the agent once at this commit with this input and judge the result."""
        sha = resolve(self.repo, ref)
        started, clock = time.monotonic(), time.time()
        with self._locks["#"]:
            self._count += 1
            # The agent writes WHODUNIT_CASE into its trace, so a number after the case id lets
            # one replay be matched to exactly one run afterwards.
            tag = f"{self.case.id}/{self._first + self._count}" if self.case.id else ""
        problem = self.build(sha)
        if problem:
            verdict, reason = SKIP, problem
        else:
            cwd = self.worktree(sha) / self.case.target
            command = [part.replace("{input}", case_input.text) for part in self.case.run]
            try:
                done = run_command(command, cwd, self._env(sha, tag), self.case.timeout)
                passed, reason = judge(self.case, case_input, done.stdout, cwd)
                if not passed and done.returncode != 0:
                    reason = f"exit {done.returncode}: " + ((done.stderr.strip().splitlines() or [reason])[-1])
                verdict = PASS if passed else FAIL
            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
                verdict, reason = FAIL, f"timed out after {self.case.timeout:.0f}s"
        result = Replay(sha=sha, input=case_input.text, verdict=verdict, reason=reason, seconds=time.monotonic() - started, started=clock, tag=tag)
        self.replays.append(result)
        return result

    def test_commit(self, ref: str) -> tuple[str, list[Replay]]:
        """Every input once. The commit fails if any input fails, and is skipped if it will not build."""
        results = []
        for case_input in self.case.inputs:
            result = self.replay(ref, case_input)
            results.append(result)
            if result.verdict != PASS:
                return result.verdict, results
        return PASS, results

    def trial(self, ref: str) -> str:
        """One replay at this commit, taking the case inputs in turn. This is what the statistical bisect calls."""
        sha = resolve(self.repo, ref)
        with self._locks[sha]:
            turn = self._turn[sha]
            self._turn[sha] += 1
        return self.replay(sha, self.case.inputs[turn % len(self.case.inputs)]).verdict

    if len(diff) > MAX_DIFF:
        diff = diff[:MAX_DIFF] + "\n[diff cut here]\n"
    evidence = Evidence(culprit=full, parent=parent, subject=subject, diff=diff, after=code_after(repo, full, target))
    if motive:
        evidence.checkpoint, evidence.request, evidence.message = motive.checkpoint, motive.request, motive.message
        evidence.steps = [asdict(s) for s in motive.steps]
    if mcp is None:
        evidence.notes.append("neatroots was not asked for runs.")
        return evidence
    try:
        runs = replay_runs(mcp, case_id)
        order = order or [full]
        at = order.index(full) if full in order else 0
        rank = {sha: n for n, sha in enumerate(order)}
        rank.setdefault(parent, -1)
        failing = sorted((r for r in replays if r["verdict"] == "fail" and rank.get(r["sha"], -9) >= at), key=lambda r: rank[r["sha"]])
        for replay in failing:
            run = _match_run(runs, replay, replays)
            if run is None:
                continue
            passing = sorted(
                (r for r in replays if r["verdict"] == "pass" and r["input"] == replay["input"] and -1 <= rank.get(r["sha"], -9) < at),
                key=lambda r: -rank[r["sha"]],
            )
            other = next((m for m in (_match_run(runs, r, replays) for r in passing) if m), None)
            evidence.failing_run = {"trace_id": run["trace_id"], "commit": run["commit"], "input": replay["input"], "reason": replay["reason"],
                                    "outline": mcp.call("get_run_outline", trace_id=run["trace_id"])["outline"]}
            if other:
                evidence.passing_run = {"trace_id": other["trace_id"], "commit": other["commit"], "input": replay["input"],
                                        "outline": mcp.call("get_run_outline", trace_id=other["trace_id"])["outline"]}
                compared = mcp.call("compare_runs", a=other["trace_id"], b=run["trace_id"])
                evidence.comparison = compared if isinstance(compared, str) else json.dumps(compared, indent=1)[:3000]
            break
        if evidence.failing_run is None:
            evidence.notes.append("No failing replay could be matched to a run in neatroots.")
        elif evidence.passing_run is None:
            evidence.notes.append("No passing replay of the same input before the culprit could be matched to a run in neatroots.")
    except (NeatError, KeyError, TypeError) as exc:
        evidence.notes.append(f"neatroots could not supply runs: {exc}")
    return evidence


def code_after(repo: str | Path, sha: str, target: str, around: int = 10, limit: int = 4000) -> str:
    """The lines each hunk touched, as they read after the commit, numbered and with their indentation intact.

    A diff's leading + and - columns make indentation easy to misread, and indentation is often the bug.
    """
    out = []
    names = [f for f in git(repo, "diff-tree", "--no-commit-id", "--name-only", "-r", sha, "--", target).split("\n") if f]
    for name in names:
        try:
            lines = git(repo, "show", f"{sha}:{name}").split("\n")
        except RuntimeError:
            continue  # the commit deleted this file
        for start, count in re.findall(r"^@@ -\d+(?:,\d+)? \+(\d+)(?:,(\d+))? @@", git(repo, "show", "--format=", "--unified=0", sha, "--", name), flags=re.M):
            first = max(1, int(start) - around)
            last = min(len(lines), int(start) + int(count or 1) + around)
            out.append(f"{name}, lines {first} to {last} after the commit:\n" + "\n".join(f"{n:>4}  {lines[n - 1]}" for n in range(first, last + 1)))
    return "\n\n".join(out)[:limit]


SYSTEM = """You write the root-cause brief for a regression in an AI agent. You are given the commit that a bisect \
named as the culprit, what the coding agent was asked to do in that commit, and a failing run next to a passing run.

Rules:
- Say which commit did it and why first. Then say how the failure shows up in the failing run.
- Use only what the evidence shows. If the evidence does not show something, do not say it.
- Read the diff line by line before describing it, including its indentation. If the bug fails only some of the time, say what in the code or the run makes it intermittent, or say that the evidence does not show why.
- Every sentence must cite at least one id from the list of citable ids: a span id, a commit, a checkpoint or a session step.
- If the request behind the commit is on record, give one sentence that sets what was asked for against what the commit did, and says where the two part ways. Cite the checkpoint.
- Plain words, short sentences, no hype. Seven sentences at most.

Answer with JSON only, in this shape:
{"headline": "one line, under 90 characters", "sentences": [{"text": "...", "cites": ["id", "id"]}]}"""


def prompt_for(evidence: Evidence, symptom: str) -> str:
    parts = [
        f"Symptom: {symptom}",
        f"Culprit commit: {evidence.culprit[:12]} \"{evidence.subject}\" (parent {evidence.parent[:12]})",
        f"What the bisect measured: {evidence.measured or 'not recorded'}",
        f"Entire checkpoint: {evidence.checkpoint or 'none'}",
        f"What the coding agent was asked: {evidence.request or 'not recorded'}",
        f"What the commit message says: {evidence.message or 'nothing beyond the subject'}",
        "Session steps between that request and the commit:\n" + ("\n".join(
            f"[{s['id']}] {s['kind']}{' ' + s['file'] if s.get('file') else ''}: {s['text'][:400]}" for s in evidence.steps[-25:]) or "none recorded"),
        "Diff of the culprit commit:\n" + evidence.diff,
        "The changed code as it reads after the commit:\n" + (evidence.after or "not available"),
    ]
    for label, run in (("Failing run", evidence.failing_run), ("Passing run", evidence.passing_run)):
        if run:
            parts.append(f"{label} {run['trace_id'][:12]} at commit {run['commit'][:12]}, input: {run['input']}\n{run['outline']}")
    if evidence.comparison:
        parts.append("neatroots comparison, passing run first:\n" + evidence.comparison)
    parts.append("Citable ids: " + ", ".join(sorted(evidence.citable())))
    return "\n\n".join(parts)


def check_citations(brief: dict, evidence: Evidence) -> dict:
    """Keep only sentences whose citations are real. A cite matches by prefix in either direction."""
    allowed = evidence.citable()

    def real(cite: str) -> str | None:
        cite = str(cite).strip().strip("[]`")
        if len(cite) < 6:
            return None
        return next((a for a in allowed if a.startswith(cite) or cite.startswith(a)), None)

    kept, dropped = [], []
    for sentence in brief.get("sentences", []):
        cites = sorted({c for c in (real(c) for c in sentence.get("cites", [])) if c})
        (kept if cites and sentence.get("text", "").strip() else dropped).append({"text": sentence.get("text", "").strip(), "cites": cites})
    return {"headline": str(brief.get("headline", "")).strip(), "sentences": kept, "dropped": [d["text"] for d in dropped]}


def template_brief(evidence: Evidence, symptom: str) -> dict:
    """A brief with no model: the facts in fixed sentences, each with its citation."""
    culprit = evidence.culprit[:12]
    sentences = [{"text": f"The failures start at commit {culprit}, \"{evidence.subject}\".", "cites": [culprit]}]
    if evidence.request and evidence.checkpoint:
        asked = evidence.request.strip().splitlines()[0][:200]
        sentences.append({"text": f"That commit came from a coding session that was asked: \"{asked}\"", "cites": [evidence.checkpoint]})
    elif evidence.message:
        sentences.append({"text": f"No coding session could be read for that commit. Its own message says: \"{evidence.message.splitlines()[0][:200]}\"", "cites": [culprit]})
    else:
        sentences.append({"text": "No coding session is recorded for that commit, so the request behind it is unknown.", "cites": [culprit]})
    if evidence.failing_run:
        run = evidence.failing_run
        sentences.append({"text": f"In a failing replay of \"{run['input']}\", {run['reason']}.", "cites": [run["trace_id"][:12]]})
    if evidence.passing_run:
        run = evidence.passing_run
        sentences.append({"text": f"The same input passed one step earlier, at commit {run['commit'][:12]}.", "cites": [run["trace_id"][:12], run["commit"][:12]]})
    return {"headline": f"{evidence.subject}: {symptom}"[:90], "sentences": sentences, "dropped": [], "model": "none, fixed template"}


def write_brief(evidence: Evidence, symptom: str) -> dict:
    """Ask the model for the brief and check its citations. Falls back to the template, and says so."""
    if llm.choice() == "none":
        return template_brief(evidence, symptom)
    try:
        answer = llm.ask(SYSTEM, prompt_for(evidence, symptom))
        found = re.search(r"\{.*\}", answer, flags=re.S)
        brief = check_citations(json.loads(found.group(0)), evidence)
    except (llm.LlmError, AttributeError, json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError) as exc:
        fallback = template_brief(evidence, symptom)
        fallback["model"] = f"none, fixed template (the model step failed: {exc})"
        return fallback
    if not brief["sentences"]:
        fallback = template_brief(evidence, symptom)
        fallback["model"] = "none, fixed template (the model's sentences had no valid citations)"
        fallback["dropped"] = brief["dropped"]
        return fallback
    brief["model"] = llm.model_name()
    return brief

286	    if args.answer is None and rulings.recall(Path.cwd(), kind) is None and not sys.stdin.isatty():
287	        # Nobody is at the keyboard. Put the question on the page and stop.
288	        print(rulings.question(kind, culprit["subject"], request))
289	        record["ruling_question"] = {"kind": kind, "question": rulings.question(kind, culprit["subject"], request)}
290	        save_record(path, record)

292	    try:
293	        decided, asked = rulings.decide(Path.cwd(), kind, case.id, culprit["sha"], culprit["subject"], request, answer=args.answer)
294	    except (ValueError, EOFError, OSError) as exc:
295	        print(f"No ruling recorded: {exc}")
296	        return 2
297	    record["ruling"] = {**asdict(decided), "asked_now": asked}
298	    save_record(path, record)
299	    print(f"Kind of change: {kind}. Ruling: {decided.ruling}." + ("" if asked else f" Decided on {decided.decided_on} in case {decided.first_case}, so nobody was asked again."))
300	    return 0

303	def _sides(record: dict) -> tuple[tuple[int, int], tuple[int, int]]:
304	    """(failures, passes) the lineup saw before the culprit, and from it onward."""
305	    order = {s["sha"]: n for n, s in enumerate(record["suspects"])}
306	    at = order[record["lineup"]["culprit"]["sha"]]
307	    good, bad = [0, 0], [0, 0]
308	    for replay in record.get("replays", []):
309	        if replay["verdict"] in ("pass", "fail"):
310	            side = bad if order.get(replay["sha"], -1) >= at else good
311	            side[0 if replay["verdict"] == "fail" else 1] += 1
312	    return tuple(good), tuple(bad)

315	def _attempt(kind: str, case, repo: Path, record: dict, args, feedback: str = "") -> dict:
316	    """Make one fix and replay it. Returns what was tried and how it went."""
317	    culprit = record["lineup"]["culprit"]["sha"]
318	    if kind == rulings.REVERT:
319	        made = fixes.revert(repo, culprit, record["case"]["bad"], case.id)
320	    else:
321	        made = fixes.patch(repo, culprit, record["case"]["bad"], case.id, case.target, (record.get("motive") or {}).get("request"), record.get("brief"), feedback)
322	    attempt = asdict(made)
323	    if made.commit is None:
324	        print(f"  {kind}: no fix was made. {made.note}")
325	        return attempt
326	    print(f"  {kind}: committed as {made.commit[:12]} on branch {made.branch}. Replaying to check it.")
327	    good, bad = _sides(record)
328	    with Runner(repo, case, keep=getattr(args, "keep", False)) as runner:
329	        checked = fixes.verify(lambda: runner.trial(made.commit), good, bad, budget=args.fix_budget, parallel=args.parallel)
330	        attempt["failed_replays"] = [f"{r.input} -> {r.reason}" for r in runner.replays if r.verdict == FAIL][:4]
331	    attempt["verification"] = asdict(checked)
332	    attempt["diff"] = git(repo, "show", "--format=", made.commit)[:4000]
333	    print(f"  {kind}: {checked.failures} failures in {checked.replays} replays. Probability the failure rate is back to where it was: {checked.probability:.1%}." + (f" Not proven: {checked.note}." if checked.note else ""))
334	    return attempt

337	def _proven(attempt: dict) -> bool:
338	    return bool((attempt.get("verification") or {}).get("fixed"))

341	def fix(args) -> int:
342	    """Apply the ruling on a branch and replay until the evidence says fixed. If it is not, try again.
343	
344	    A patch that is not proven gets one more try, with the first patch and its failing replays
345	    in front of the model. If that is not proven either, the culprit is reverted, which is the
346	    safe answer and loses what the commit was for. Every try is kept in the record.
347	    """
348	    loaded = _need_culprit(args)
349	    if loaded is None:
350	        return 2
351	    case, repo, record, path = loaded
352	    if not record.get("ruling"):
353	        print(f"No ruling yet. Run `whodunit ruling {args.case}` first.")
354	        return 2
355	    wanted = record["ruling"]["ruling"]
356	    attempts = [_attempt(wanted, case, repo, record, args)]
357	    if wanted == rulings.PATCH and not _proven(attempts[-1]):
358	        first = attempts[-1]
359	        feedback = (first.get("note") or "") + "\nThe first patch:\n" + first.get("diff", "none was made") + "\nReplays of it that still failed:\n" + "\n".join(first.get("failed_replays", []) or ["none recorded"])
360	        print("  The patch is not proven. Trying once more, with the first patch and its failures in view.")
361	        attempts.append(_attempt(rulings.PATCH, case, repo, record, args, feedback))
362	    if wanted == rulings.PATCH and not _proven(attempts[-1]):
363	        print("  Still not proven. Falling back to a revert, which loses what the commit was for.")
364	        attempts.append(_attempt(rulings.REVERT, case, repo, record, args))
365	        attempts[-1]["note"] = ((attempts[-1].get("note") or "") + " This is a fallback: the ruling was to patch, and two patches were not proven.").strip()
366	    final = next((a for a in reversed(attempts) if _proven(a)), attempts[-1])
367	    record["fix"] = final
368	    record["attempts"] = attempts
369	    if _proven(final):
370	        kept = Path.cwd() / "cases" / f"{case.id}.toml"
371	        kept.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
372	        text = Path(args.case).read_text().rstrip("\n")
373	        if "\nfixed = " in "\n" + text:
374	            text = "\n".join(line for line in text.splitlines() if not line.startswith(("fixed = ", "# Closed by Whodunit")))
375	        # Top-level keys have to come before the first table in TOML, so the line goes at the top.
376	        text = f'# Closed by Whodunit. Replay with `whodunit check cases/{case.id}.toml`.\nfixed = "{final["commit"]}"\n' + text
377	        kept.write_text(text + "\n")
378	        record["fix"]["regression_case"] = os.path.relpath(kept)
379	    save_record(path, record)
380	    if _proven(final):
381	        print(f"Fixed by {final['kind']} {final['commit'][:12]} after {len(attempts)} {'try' if len(attempts) == 1 else 'tries'}. Kept as a regression test: {record['fix']['regression_case']}")
382	        print(f"The branch {final['branch']} is local. Pushing it and opening a pull request is the owner's call.")
383	    else:
384	        print(f"Not fixed after {len(attempts)} {'try' if len(attempts) == 1 else 'tries'}. The record has each one.")
385	    return 0 if _proven(final) else 1

388	def investigate(args) -> int:
389	    """Run a whole case: lineup, motive and brief, ruling, fix, damages, case file. Stops only for the owner's ruling."""
390	    import time

404	    if getattr(args, "fresh", False) and path.is_file():
405	        path.rename(path.with_name(path.name + time.strftime(".%H%M%S.old")))
406	    record = load_record(path)
407	    args.method, args.confidence, args.no_priors, args.keep, args.json = "statistical", 0.95, False, False, False
408	    args.repeats = 1
409	    args.no_runs, args.since_ms = False, None
410	    if not (record.get("lineup") or {}).get("culprit"):
411	        args.resume = bool(record.get("replays"))
412	        code = lineup(args)

428	    code = ruling(args)
